objective: Diagnose the direct-label bottleneck across independently validated Paper 3 observability rounds without repeating keyword search, separating retrieval coverage, source eligibility, question-definition specificity, outcome-window structure, and trajectory missingness.

method.design: Descriptive cross-round audit of frozen cohorts and their recorded source/follow-up receipts. Round 3 was independently reconciled; Round 4 used a frozen citation-tracing plus authenticated-primary-full-text protocol; Round 5 used a fresh source-only objective-endpoint cohort and a fixed five-year future window.
denominator_rules: Source eligibility uses selected source rows as denominator; source-ineligible rows remain counted and were not future-searched.
Direct-label yield uses source-eligible questions as denominator. Not-observed, inaccessible, adjacent, proxy, same-team, or unmatched follow-ups remain unadjudicated, never negative.
Round 4 is not a new independent cohort: it re-audits the three eligible Round 3 rows and is not pooled as three additional questions.
Trajectory dimensions are counted separately from direct resolution/refutation and are not substituted for Paper 3 labels.

round3.followup_window: strictly after each year-end cutoff through cutoff year plus five years inclusive

round4.followup_window: strictly after each year-end cutoff through the inherited fixed followup end

round5.followup_window: strictly after each year-end cutoff through cutoff year plus five years inclusive

combined_source_screen_context.note: This is the separate 16-paper source-screen frame; it is not a direct-outcome denominator and was not retrospectively relabeled.

cross_round_counts.paper3_score: not_estimable; no positive/negative direct class contrast and no valid grouped temporal holdout

denominators_and_exclusions.round3: 3 eligible; the report records two rows without authenticated matched primary full text after bounded searching; the one authenticated positive trajectory was partial only.
denominators_and_exclusions.round4: 3/3 inherited rows had recorded authenticated or cross-checked follow-up source material (2, 3, and 2 source records respectively), but 0/3 matched the frozen endpoint tuple.
denominators_and_exclusions.round5: 4/6 rows had at least one follow-up source record (source counts 1, 2, 0, 1, 1, 0); 2/6 had no candidate primary follow-up in the bounded search. The 4 source-bearing rows still yielded 0/4 direct labels.
denominators_and_exclusions.prior_13_question_audit: 4/13 primary-full-text-checked; 4/13 abstract/search-visible only; 1/13 undated web only; 1/13 source/pre-cutoff only; 3/13 no candidate primary; 0/13 direct labels.

cause_comparison.observed_support: Coverage is incomplete, especially for the original 13-question audit and two Round 5 rows. Retrieval improvement is therefore required for valid ascertainment.
cause_comparison.limitation: Because all source-bearing Round 4 and Round 5 follow-ups were definition-mismatched, better retrieval alone did not produce a direct label. Search non-detection remains missingness, not evidence of unresolved science.

denominators_and_exclusions.round3: 3/4 selected rows source-eligible; 1/4 ineligible and excluded from follow-up, retained in the source-screen denominator.
denominators_and_exclusions.round5: 6/6 selected rows source-eligible under the stricter objective-endpoint rule.

cause_comparison.observed_support: Eligibility screening reliably produces source-grounded questions, but the eligible subset still has 0/9 unique direct labels across Rounds 3 and 5. Eligibility attrition is real (4/16 in the separate frame) but cannot explain the direct-label zero once eligible rows are analyzed.

denominators_and_exclusions.round4: 0/3 exact matches despite follow-up source records for all 3. QAOA sources changed postselection to GNN/recursive initialization; repair sources changed SSC to other repair/representation methods; RiverGame changed exploit reporting to broader visual/audio/gameplay testing.
denominators_and_exclusions.round5: 0/6 exact matches. The 4 source-bearing rows were adjacent or partial: explanation quality without patch-only reviewer outcomes; DNN diagnosis/performance repair without DNN-aware security-regression comparison; SERENIoT scope narrowing without matched policy efficacy; Avocado implementation/case study without matched unconstrained baseline. The two no-source rows remain missing, not mismatches.

cause_comparison.observed_support: Across 7 recorded Round 4 source records and 5 recorded Round 5 source records, none matched the frozen tuple sufficiently for a direct label. Round 5's more objective source definitions improved trajectory coding (3 partial-progress and 2 scope-narrowing records) but did not improve direct-label yield from the Round 4 baseline of 0/3 to 0/6.

denominators_and_exclusions.window: All three rounds used fixed five-year post-cutoff windows; Round 3 and Round 5 explicitly bound admissible evidence to strictly after cutoff through cutoff year plus five years inclusive.
denominators_and_exclusions.observed_windows: Round 3 spans 2017–2022, 2019–2024, and 2020–2025 among eligible rows; Round 5 spans 2018–2023, 2019–2024, and 2020–2025.

cause_comparison.observed_support: No matched direct result was authenticated near or just beyond a window boundary. The prior bottleneck audit likewise found no authenticated result just outside a frozen three-year window. Therefore a too-short window is neither established nor falsified.
cause_comparison.limitation: Bounded retrieval and zero matched candidates prevent a window-edge sensitivity estimate; extending the window without endpoint matching would not solve the bottleneck.

denominators_and_exclusions.round3: Among 3 eligible, 1/3 partial progress and 3/3 direct outcomes unadjudicated.
denominators_and_exclusions.round4: Among 3 audited, 3/3 partial progress and 3/3 direct outcomes unadjudicated.
denominators_and_exclusions.round5: Among 6 eligible, 3/6 partial progress, 2/6 scope narrowing, and 6/6 direct outcomes unadjudicated; 0/6 independent strengthening and 0/6 contradictory evidence.

cause_comparison.observed_support: The rubric can observe non-direct trajectories while the direct outcome field remains entirely missing. This is a structural missingness problem for the Paper 3 target, not permission to collapse partial progress or scope narrowing into resolution/refutation.

observed_result_or_blocker.diagnosis: The direct-label bottleneck is primarily endpoint-definition/matching scarcity, amplified by incomplete retrieval. Source eligibility is a useful gate but not the limiting step after screening. A five-year window has not been shown inadequate. Trajectory evidence is observable, but direct outcome labels are missing by design-preserving adjudication.
blockers: No positive or negative direct label exists in the 9 unique eligible questions.
No temporal Paper 3 score, calibration, ranking metric, or forecast accuracy is identifiable.
Search non-detection and adjacent outcomes cannot be used as negative labels.

selection_steps: Sample only from the year-end-safe historical frame using deterministic hash priority and predeclared topic/year strata; do not use future citations, follow-up hits, popularity, or known outcomes.

Require the cutoff-version source to state one fixed object or property, one explicit intervention/comparator or baseline, one measurable endpoint with an independent unit/denominator, and one falsification condition.

Require the source to identify a concrete public artifact, benchmark, dataset, implementation, or formal test object available by the cutoff; reject reviewer-created generalizations and questions requiring vague human success judgments without a frozen protocol.
Prefer questions whose endpoint can be checked by an independent primary artifact and whose comparator is source-pinned; do not select merely because a later result is known.
Seal the question, endpoint, comparator, window, and exclusion rules before any future-evidence retrieval; retain source-ineligible rows in the denominator.
Use the same five-year window initially, but record year-1–2 versus year-3–5 evidence separately; do not extend or relabel a window post hoc.
next_cohort_selection_rule.falsification_gate_for_rule: If the next source-only cohort has at least 6 eligible rows, at least 4 with independently checkable public artifacts, and still produces 0 exact direct matches despite authenticated primary follow-up coverage for at least 5/6, stop further retrieval-focused cohort expansion and declare the direct-label transfer infeasible under the current Paper 3 rubric; pursue a separately preregistered experiment instead.
next_cohort_selection_rule.why_changed: Rounds 3–5 show that objective wording alone does not overcome endpoint mismatch. The next rule adds source-pinned artifact/comparator requirements while preserving point-in-time selection and no hindsight relabeling.

next_falsifiable_action: Apply PAPER3-DIRECT-ENDPOINT-COHORT-V1 to a new deterministic source-only cohort, then independently audit dated primary artifacts against the exact endpoint tuple and split evidence by window phase. The claim that formulation/matching is the main bottleneck is falsified if this artifact/comparator-gated cohort yields materially higher exact-match coverage than 0/9; the claim that retrieval is sufficient is falsified if authenticated coverage remains high while exact matches remain zero.
uncertainty: These are deterministic, bounded cohorts rather than representative CS population samples.
Round 4 is an independent retrieval audit but not an independent question cohort.
Authenticated source availability and candidate counts are receipts of the bounded protocols, not estimates of all published evidence.
The cause comparison is descriptive and cannot establish causal attribution among correlated retrieval and formulation mechanisms.
No direct outcome prevalence or Paper 3 predictive performance is claimed.
state_queue_ledger_status: not edited; supervisor-owned state, queue, ledger, and status preserved
